in_sanskrit.name: बिनिता
in_sanskrit.meaning: Bindu (dot) or Bindu (boundary) + ता (feminine form of ता, meaning 'she')
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: Goddess of binding or limiting, as in the limiting of a woman's emotions or desires. Also, Bindu is a term in Hinduism for the point at the center of the universe, representing the divine presence. Binita can be seen as a symbol of the divine feminine that both limits and binds, and is also connected to the divine presence within.

in_hindi.name: बिनिता
in_hindi.meaning: बिनदी (बिन = bindu, दा = tā, न = feminine suffix) or बिनाती (बिन = bindu, ती = tā)
in_hindi.long_meaning: Binita is a name derived from the Sanskrit term 'bindu,' which means a dot or a point. In the context of Hinduism, 'bindu' can also refer to the central point or the divine presence. The feminine form 'tā' is added to 'bindu,' resulting in the name Binita. The name can be interpreted as a symbol of the divine feminine that both limits and binds, and is also connected to the divine presence within.
